scripts.build: pnpm --filter @southleft/al-web-components build && pnpm --filter @southleft/sl-web-components build && pnpm --filter @southleft/al-react build
scripts.//build:app-home: PARKED 2026-08-27 - deliberately NOT in build:all, so apps/home is not deployed. The site root redirects to /docs/ instead (pages-root/_redirects). The script is kept so the app can still be built locally if it is ever revived or rewritten; nothing in CI runs it, so treat it as unbuilt code. The root-level files it used to ship (_headers, _redirects, favicon.ico) now live in pages-root/ and are copied by copy:pages-root - see pages-root/README.md for why that move was required.
scripts.//copy:pages-root: Copies pages-root/ into dist/ - the files Cloudflare reads ONLY from the published root (_headers, _redirects) plus the root favicon. Runs after build:app-docs because it needs dist/ to exist.
scripts.build:fixtures: pnpm run build:app-web-components && pnpm run build:app-react && pnpm run build:app-mfe && pnpm run build:app-ssr && pnpm run build:story-fixture
scripts.//build:all: THE CLOUDFLARE PAGES DEPLOY COMMAND (build output directory: dist). Order is load-bearing, not alphabetical: this is a strict && chain, so the first non-zero exit leaves dist/ in whatever state it had reached and Cloudflare publishes nothing. THE product surface is the docs site, so it builds IMMEDIATELY after the libraries it depends on, ahead of the angular/react/svelte/astro/southleft fixture apps, which nothing in dist/docs depends on. A broken demo fixture must not be able to take the documentation site down with it. copy:pages-root follows it and ships the files Cloudflare reads only from the published root (_headers, _redirects) - it needs dist/ to already exist, which is why it is not first. NOTE apps/home (the homepage that used to own dist/index.html and serve `/`) was dropped from this chain on 2026-08-27; the root now 302s to /docs/ via pages-root/_redirects, and nothing writes dist/index.html. Reordering remains safe because no step clears the shared dist/ root: every app clears only its own subdirectory.
scripts.build:all: pnpm run build && pnpm run build:app-docs && pnpm run copy:components && pnpm run copy:pages-root && pnpm run build:app-angular && pnpm run build:app-react && pnpm run build:app-svelte && pnpm run build:app-astro && pnpm run build:app-southleft
scripts.//parity:projection: Builds the TRACKED projection of the gitignored canvas dumps (.altitude/figma-sync/canvas-projection.json) so contract-diff can compute the same property-level disagreements in CI and on the deployed docs site, where the dumps do not exist. Without it that layer compared ZERO pairs, which rendered identically to zero disagreements. Verified byte-identical to the live dumps: 36 pairs, 259 disagreements. Carries names only - node ids, file keys, paths and every number are scrubbed and the scrub is asserted. Regenerate after contracts:canvas; gate with parity:projection:check.
scripts.//contracts:emit: T10 (spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation): contracts under .altitude/contracts/ are now EDITABLE SOURCE, not a derived artifact — this script no longer overwrites them by default. Bare `contracts:emit` / `contracts:emit:sl` now just print a usage note pointing at the modes below. See .altitude/contracts/README.md.
scripts.//contracts:seed: Bootstraps a contract for a NEW parity-tracked component only — refuses to overwrite an existing (hand-edited) contract file unless --force.
scripts.//contracts:check: Contract<->code DRIFT CHECK (--check-drift): re-derives every tracked component from its sources (CEM, manifest, token-map, measure-components output) and diffs it against the on-disk contract, excluding status/version (curation metadata) and, when this environment has no spec-light.json, the anatomy-dependent fields too (see .altitude/contracts/README.md "Anatomy availability is best-effort"). Exit 1 on any drift. Pass --project <id> for another design system; contract<->canvas drift is `contracts:diff` instead.
scripts.//contracts:validate: Contract SCHEMA validation (--check): ajv-validates the on-disk contracts against contract.schema.json, read-only. Refuses an illegal contract file BY NAME (path + failing rule) rather than a bare exit code.
scripts.//contracts:check-determinism: T15 (spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation): re-derives every tracked component's contract TWICE in memory (no disk/git involved) and byte-compares the two serializations — same contract inputs must produce byte-identical output. Exit 1 + names any component whose two derivations differ.
scripts.//contracts:ops-determinism: T12 (spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation) — the 'ops' half of R7's byte-identical claim the T15 TODO left open: derives the al-button contract's Figma ops artifact (generate-figma.mjs's buildOps()) TWICE in memory and byte-compares the two serializations. Scoped to al-button as the canary; since the 2026-08-26 modularization the same derivation (scripts/contracts/figma/derive-ops.mjs) runs for every contract (--component <tag> --ops-only verified across the full roster), so widening this check is a script-loop away if ever needed.
scripts.//gate:contracts: T15/T20 (spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation) — the CI contract gate, five legs, both projects where applicable: (a) contracts:validate[:sl] -- ajv schema validation, refuses an illegal contract BY NAME; (b) contracts:check[:sl] -- --check-drift, CEM-derived API (props/events/slots/a11y/bindings) diffed against the on-disk contract; (c) contracts:check-determinism[:sl] -- same contract inputs -> byte-identical serialized output, independent of git; (d) contracts:ops-determinism -- T12's Figma ops half of the same claim, pilot-scoped (al-button, altitude only -- no Figma connection needed, this checks the ops DERIVATION, not a live build); (e) check:contract-docs[:sl] -- T20's generated per-component reference docs (.altitude/contracts/docs/<project>/<tag>.md) diffed against what the contracts + parity manifest would produce, byte-for-byte, orphans included.
scripts.gate:contracts: pnpm run contracts:validate && pnpm run contracts:validate:sl && pnpm run contracts:check && pnpm run contracts:check:sl && pnpm run contracts:check-determinism && pnpm run contracts:check-determinism:sl && pnpm run contracts:ops-determinism && pnpm run check:contract-docs && pnpm run check:contract-docs:sl
scripts.//contracts:canvas: Extracts CANVAS contracts (variant axes, component properties, bound-variable names, text styles, states, shallow anatomy) from live Figma component sets over scripts/figma-atoms/mcp-shim.mjs into .altitude/figma-sync/<project>/canvas-contracts/. See .altitude/contracts/canvas-contract.schema.json. --component <tag> extracts one set; --from-fixture runs offline against scripts/contracts/__fixtures__/canvas-sample.json.
scripts.//contracts:diff: Property-level CODE <-> CANVAS contract diff (T6, contract-diff.mjs) for one tag or --all: which props/variant values/states/token bindings disagree, degradation-aware. Missing canvas dump -> one clean line, exit 0. --json for machine output; --self-test runs the offline acceptance test against __fixtures__/diff-*-sample.*.json.
scripts.//contracts:docs: T20 (spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation) — builds the per-component Markdown reference doc at .altitude/contracts/docs/<project>/<tag>.md from each tracked component's contract + that project's parity manifest (structure, props, variant axes, slots + placeholder convention, states, token bindings incl. conditionalBindings, Figma set name/nodeId or the by-name resolution rule for a set with no pinned id). GENERATED — do not hand-edit; check:contract-docs is the drift gate (see build-component-docs.mjs's header and .altitude/contracts/README.md).
scripts.//gate:docs: Runs the SCOPE gate first: check:sl-scope re-derives each scoped design system's library.components allowlist from its own site's source, which is what makes 'adding a component to the site is what earns it a docs page' true. Then the docs coverage gate, which proves every component in the manifest has a generated page and every project's scope resolves.
scripts.gate:docs: pnpm run check:sl-scope && pnpm --filter al-app-docs check:coverage
scripts.//gate:docs-generalises: Runs a THROWAWAY third design-system project through the same functions the real sites are built from, and greps apps/docs/src for any project id, to prove a new client brand costs a registry entry and no code. Needs no build.
scripts.//gate:docs-panels: Runs AFTER `pnpm --filter al-app-docs build` — it reads the built html in dist/docs to prove the status panels shipped no Figma file keys, node ids or internal script paths, and that every rendered status matches what the parity engine and the axe report say.
scripts.//gate:guidance: Runs AFTER `pnpm --filter al-app-docs build`. The generated half of the docs has gates; this covers the AUTHORED half — the component guidance in apps/docs/src/content/guidance. It fails when guidance is written for something that is not a component, when a component page states neither guidance nor its absence, when a rendered panel is missing a required section (notably `when not to use`), when a cited file or its anchor text no longer exists, or when authored coverage drops below the floor.
scripts.//story-fixture: Renders every component story with real Lit — the accessibility sweep's fixture, replacing the storybook-static build. Same index.json + iframe.html?id= + #storybook-root contract. NOTE it is built through the al-web-components workspace package rather than `--dir`: story-fixture/ is nested inside that package, so `libs/*` does not match it, it has no node_modules of its own, and `pnpm --dir ... exec vite` finds no vite on a clean CI install.
scripts.a11y:report:fixture: pnpm run build:story-fixture && node scripts/build-a11y-report.mjs --storybook libs/al-web-components/story-fixture/dist
scripts.//a11y:report: Regenerates .altitude/a11y/report.json, which the docs accessibility panels read. Prefer `a11y:report:fixture`, which builds the story fixture and points this at it. The --storybook flag keeps its name for compatibility; it takes any directory serving the index.json + iframe.html?id= contract. Never point it at a dev server (see the measurement note in scripts/build-a11y-report.mjs).
scripts.//a11y:report:docs: Regenerates .altitude/a11y/report-docs.json - axe against the BUILT docs site, for components the story fixture does not cover (today: the Southleft brand layer, which has no stories of its own). Build the site first: pnpm --filter al-app-docs build. Measures each component's DEFAULT story only - the panel states that rather than implying full coverage.
scripts.//test:scripts: The offline, zero-dependency self-tests under scripts/__tests__/. These existed and NOTHING RAN THEM — the same rot that let libs/altitude-mcp/test/smoke.mjs drift until it asserted 6 of 8 tools (see the mcp-smoke job's own comment). They need no pnpm install and no browser, so they run in the gate-self-test CI job. check-brand-conformance.test.mjs is deliberately NOT in this list: it fails today against the real al-header/al-footer public-surface gaps, which is why check:brand-conformance is warning-only in CI — adding it here would gate on a known-open issue rather than on a regression.
scripts.test:scripts: node scripts/__tests__/parity-receipt.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/pinned-nodes.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/figma-conventions.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/visual-facts.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/drift-mutations.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/reconcile-eval.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/direction-eval.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/curation-eval.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/trajectory.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/judgement-ledger.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/trap-index.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/vision-calibration.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/check-figma-drift.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/component-check.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/check-doc-anchors.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/validate-usage.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/check-api-vocabulary.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/check-cem-render.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/run-gates.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/component-evidence.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/check-context-budget.test.mjs && node scripts/__tests__/canvas-projection.test.mjs
scripts.//evals:drift-cases: T5 (spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals) — builds the RECONCILIATION EVAL CORPUS from the repo's own tracked contracts. For every component with both a code contract and an extracted canvas contract, it applies each named deterministic mutation from scripts/ai-readiness/lib/drift-mutations.mjs and records what contract-diff.mjs says disagrees. That is the answer key: no human labelling and no LLM in the grading path. 120 cases across 35 components today. NOT A CI GATE and it cannot be one: canvas contracts are gitignored live observations (.gitignore:122) and are absent on a clone, so --check only works on a machine that has run `contracts:canvas`. The tracked corpus at .altitude/ai-readiness/drift-cases.altitude.json is therefore the durable artifact, and its invariants ARE checked in CI, by scripts/__tests__/drift-mutations.test.mjs via test:scripts.
scripts.//evals:vision-calibration: T10 (spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals, R6) — may a vision judge screen visual fidelity yet? Reads .altitude/ai-readiness/vision-calibration.json and refuses to certify below the threshold (12 balanced labelled cases, 75% agreement). Bare invocation REPORTS and exits 0; --certify is the assertion and exits 1 when not certified. CURRENTLY BLOCKED and the reason is the finding: the labelled cases do not exist. .altitude/visual-compare/auto/ is gitignored run output, and the one documented visual defect (al-toggle`s giant square) lost its evidence when the fix regenerated the PNG in place — visual defects here erase their own evidence as they are repaired, so the set has to be captured at the moment a defect is found, not assembled afterwards. The judge itself is deliberately NOT written: shipping a vision-model call nobody can calibrate would be shipping the unverifiable half and skipping the half that decides whether it may be trusted.
scripts.//evals:traps: T9 (spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals) — inventories the numbered TRAPS in the four Figma skills and reports how many are cited by an eval case. MEASURED: 52 traps (generate 15, repair 14, snippet 10, sync 13), not the ~70 an early estimate claimed. Coverage is by CITATION — a case`s `source` must name the skill and the trap number — never by resemblance, because a coverage number produced by string similarity drifts up whenever a case is reworded. The number is a GAP REPORT and is meant to be low; --check is a drift gate on the tracked index. Runs offline; the skills are tracked so it works on a clone.
scripts.//check:judgement-ledger: T12 (spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals, R8) — is .altitude/judgement-ledger.json still true? Two offline checks: every ledger point's anchor string still resolves in the file it names (so an entry cannot go on describing something that moved or was deleted), and every source file carrying one of this repo's own judgement-call markers ('judgment call', 'decide with a human', 'not a derivable fact') either backs a ledger point or is listed in markerFilesAcknowledged. The 13 points were found by a ONE-OFF sweep; nothing would have surfaced the 14th, which is what this gate is for. File-level, not line-level, deliberately: line numbers churn on every edit and a checker that cries wolf gets turned off. Zero-dependency, runs in the gate-self-test CI job.
scripts.//check:figma-conventions: T3 (spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals) — the library conventions buildAiPrompt() tells an agent to apply BY HAND (Title Case axis names/values/properties, the State axis vocabulary, set name vs the manifest), linted OFFLINE over the extracted canvas contracts. ITS FIRST RUN found two genuine defects (al-banner's placeholder BOOLEAN property 'Is everything all good?' and al-divider's 'State=Verical'). BOTH ARE NOW CLEAN — verified live 2026-08-29: 37 contracts, 0 violations. They had in fact ALREADY been fixed in Figma; the lint was reading a canvas snapshot extracted 2026-08-27 and so reported two-day-stale defects as current. It prints the oldest extraction timestamp on every run for exactly this reason — read that line before believing a violation. STILL NOT IN CI, and fixing those two was NOT the blocker: canvas contracts are gitignored live observations, absent on a clone, and this script correctly exits 1 when it finds none rather than passing vacuously — so as a CI gate it would fail every run on principle. Same structural constraint as evals:drift-cases --check. Gating it would need a TRACKED projection of the conventions, not the gitignored contracts. Variant ORDER and page name stay deliberately out of its reach and it says so on every run — extract-canvas.mjs sorts axis options, so on-canvas order is not in the artifact.
scripts.//parity:pins: T2 (spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals) — are the manifest's PINNED Figma node ids still live? getNodeByIdAsync returns a DETACHED node after its page is deleted (removed === false, parent chain reaches no PAGE), so 'it resolved' is not proof it is in the document: 11 of 20 pinned ids were ghosts on 2026-08-27 and extract-canvas.mjs extracted from the ghost. extract-canvas was fixed at the point of use; the MANIFEST was not, so the stale id keeps reaching agents through buildAiPrompt() and figmaNodeUrlFor(). 34 pinned ids for altitude, 15 for southleft (the rest map by name, which cannot go stale). Needs the shim running. --repin rewrites the ids where exactly one live set carries that name; two sets sharing a name is its own trap, so that case is reported, never guessed.
scripts.//capture:docs: T-capture (owner direction 2026-08-29): ground-truth PNGs of EVERY component in the docs and EVERY variant of each, driven through the docs Playground own enum + boolean controls. The acceptance reference for base Altitude is the DOCS, not the isolated harness (measure-components.mjs, fixture content, default state only) and not a single element (capture-site.mjs). Needs the docs served: pnpm --filter al-app-docs start, or serve the built dist/ and pass --url. Axes are walked INDEPENDENTLY, never as a cartesian product. A component that paints nothing until a boolean flips (al-alert until isActive) gets a VISIBLE BASELINE found automatically and recorded per shot. Hosts that are display:contents have a 0x0 box, so the mount is shot instead and shotOf records which. Every failure is written to index.json with its reason - a missing shot must never read as a passing one.
scripts.//check:contract-fidelity: Is a contract a faithful enough description of its component to REBUILD it? Written 2026-08-29 after a regeneration sweep replaced good Figma sets with bare boxes while every variant-count and axis-name comparison passed. GATES on a ZERO-WIDTH root box, which is not a small measurement but the absence of one - it happens to every width:100%/flex:1 component measured in an unconstrained harness (repair skill trap 12) and generating from one cannot produce anything but a degenerate set. 17 contracts are in that state today. REPORTS (never gates) the structure shortfall between contract anatomy and what the docs actually render, because a docs page mounts a realistic composition and legitimately has more nodes - gating on it would be the eleven-false-positive lesson again. Needs pnpm run capture:docs first; refuses to run without that ground truth rather than passing vacuously. generate-figma.mjs enforces the same zero-width rule per component before it writes.
scripts.//docs:compare: Renders every project's BUILT docs (dist/docs — run `pnpm --filter al-app-docs build` first) and asserts the docs↔site parity facts from spec 2026-08-28-southleft-docs-parity-with-example-site: registry-driven default mode + contrast on the brand host, the display heading computing the brand's own preset face (guards the :root-alias trap that shipped IBM Plex headings under every brand), al-layout upgraded with the overview hero resolved to a multi-track grid, and zero page errors — then writes .altitude/visual-compare/docs-<project>[-detail].png for eyeball comparison against each design system's own site. Before this, nothing in the repo screenshotted a docs page.
scripts.//test:contrast-axis: Behavioural verification for <al-theme contrast> (spec 2026-08-22-token-debt-and-machine-readable-metadata). Proves contrast='more' raises --al-theme-opacity-disabled on a REAL rendered component and clears WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1) against the worst realistic disabled pairing in both modes, and that nesting a bare or explicit contrast="normal" <al-theme> inside one set to 'more' resets rather than inherits. Served through the same Vite-dev-server + static-harness infrastructure as test:scoped-theming (`.altitude/visual-compare/harness/contrast-axis.{html,js}`), not a live Storybook — Storybook was removed from this repo 2026-08-25. Requires `pnpm --filter @southleft/al-web-components build` first; first run compiles the whole component graph on demand and can take a minute.
scripts.//check:palette-contrast: WCAG AA gate over the EMITTED semantic palette (both modes). Distinct from test:contrast-axis, which only exercises the contrast= axis against hardcoded colours and cannot see a palette re-point. Needs build:tokens first (dist-v5 is gitignored).
scripts.baselines:capture: pnpm run build && pnpm --filter al-app-web-components build && pnpm run baselines:tokens && pnpm run baselines:bundle && pnpm run baselines:vrt
scripts.//test:unit: Vitest 3 in BROWSER MODE (Playwright/chromium) over both component libraries. `wc` compiles @southleft/al-web-components from SOURCE; `react` resolves it through its exports map, i.e. dist/ - so run `pnpm run build` before `test:unit` or the React project tests a stale library. Ports 6180/6185. A min-count reporter fails the run if either project collects fewer tests than its floor.
scripts.//gate:lit-a11y: Accessibility lint over the Lit templates. Most rules are error and clean; the three that are not are pinned by a one-way ratchet so known-bad cannot grow. --ratchet tightens after a fix.
scripts.//gate:coverage: V8 code coverage against the one-way floor in .altitude/baselines/coverage.json. NOT the same thing as scripts/check-cem-coverage.js, which measures custom-elements-manifest completeness. Run test:unit:coverage first.
scripts.//lint:styles: THE HARD STYLE GATE. Stylelint over every .scss file in both component libraries and every example app (143 files, 0 violations as of 2026-08-23). Two rules only, both aimed at generated CSS: declaration-strict-value forces a var() on colour properties, value-no-unknown-custom-properties catches a hallucinated token name against the committed tokens digest. See stylelint.config.mjs.
scripts.//lint:styles:report: The same rules over the sites' hand-written .css as well. NOT a gate: 21 pre-existing violations live there (15 literal status hues in apps/docs/src/styles/docs.css, 5 in the visual-compare harness, 1 inline-set swatch property in the southleft site). They are reported, not disabled — see scripts/check-styles-changed.mjs.
scripts.//gate:styles-new: Stylelint on the lines a branch actually changed, in any .scss or .css file. This is what holds the line over the site CSS that lint:styles cannot gate. Per-PR: on a branch that has diverged far from main it approaches 'lint everything'.
scripts.//verify: THE ONE COMMAND. Runs every gate whose prerequisites are already satisfied and NAMES the ones it skipped - a skipped gate is never reported as a pass. Reads .altitude/gates.json, the declarative inventory of all 85 gates (58 in CI directly, 11 transitively, 16 local-only). Tiers are cumulative: fast needs no build, build needs the libraries, live needs a Figma shim or the network. See .altitude/GATES.md.
scripts.//gates:check-ci: DRIFT GATE on .altitude/gates.json, both directions: every `ci` job name a gate claims must exist in v2-checks.yml and actually invoke it, and every `pnpm run` the workflow invokes must be declared here. Renaming a CI job is therefore a breaking change to the manifest - which is the same rule .github/rulesets/README.md states for the required-check list, for the same reason.
scripts.//component:check: Mechanical component-deliverable checklist for one tag (or --all): bundle.ts export, migration.json entry, CEM presence+freshness, source files (blockers); parity manifest, React wrapper, guidance YAML, llms.txt, changeset (warnings). The prose flow lives in .claude/skills/altitude-component-authoring/SKILL.md.
scripts.//verify:component: Per-component evidence bundle. Writes .altitude/verification/<tag>/<run-id>.json - one row per claim with status pass|fail|unobserved, a citation naming what was read, and the measured value. `unobserved` never counts as a pass, and the verdict REFUSES to compute when the bundle is older than the source it describes. Derived from Monday Morning's verify-spec pattern: the runner assembles evidence, code computes the verdict.
scripts.//parity:freshness: Prints figmaLastRefreshed age, everObserved and unreachable statuses per DS project. Exit 0 by default (the Figma loop is deliberately operator-driven — .altitude/FIGMA-SYNC.md); --max-age-days N turns it into a gate. Wired as a warning-only CI step in repo-hygiene.
scripts.//parity:tokens-drift: Token-level Figma<->code drift: value comparison (color/dimension/shadow canonicalization), brand/mode-aware bucketing, rename detection. Takes a saved figma_export_tokens JSON: pnpm run parity:tokens-drift -- .altitude/figma-sync/last-export.json [--project <id>]. Exit 1 on any drift. The export-shape assumption is best-effort until a real export is captured — see the script header.
scripts.//check:brand-conformance: For each brandLibrary supersession (brand al-header/al-footer capturing base tags), fails if base public surface (slots/parts/cssproperties/attributes) is missing from the brand override; also reports (never fails) base components the project's scope has never considered. Warning-only in CI until the real al-header/al-footer gaps are fixed — see the open issue.
scripts.//check:mcp-docs: Asserts every hand-written surface that lists the Altitude MCP's tools (AGENTS.md, the MCP README, the southleft.com tools page) matches what server.mjs registers — the roster drifted to 'six tools' in three places while the server registered eight. check:llms guards the generated llms.txt; this guards the prose.
scripts.//check:llms: The root llms.txt is GENERATED (scripts/build-root-llms.mjs) from the committed artifacts — the CEM, the two ai-readiness digests, the axe report, the ds-project registry and the MCP server's registerTool calls. This fails when it has drifted from them, and also when any repo-relative link it emits is missing or untracked, which is what put three dead build-artifact links in the hand-written version.
scripts.//check:doc-anchors: DOCUMENTATION-ROT GATE. Every backticked repo path, `pnpm run` script, `--filter` workspace and `node script --flag` written in a Markdown doc or SKILL.md must resolve against the real tree. It exists because prose rots silently while generated docs are gated: on 2026-09-02 fourteen documents still instructed a Storybook retired on 2026-08-25, a skill step invoked a script deleted four days earlier, and WORKFLOWS.md named two scripts that do not exist. Dated exceptions live in .altitude/doc-anchors-allowlist.json; an expired one FAILS on purpose. Conservative by design - an ambiguous span is skipped and counted, never guessed at.
scripts.//check:context-budget: How many words must an agent read before it can act? Pins the always-loaded surface (CLAUDE.md + .claude/CLAUDE.md) and the read-path for a Figma-generate task, and fails on an INCREASE. Two-way like the other ratchets: a drop larger than the slack fails too, naming --update, so the pin follows real reductions instead of drifting. Today: always-loaded 2694 words; figma-generate 15,515, of which AGENTS.md is over half.
scripts.//check:figma-parse: Parses every Figma generator file. It exists because backticks inside String.raw comments broke build-set-code.mjs three times in one day, and because two skill traps are now recorded as `gated` on THIS script - a disposition that is a lie if nothing runs it.
scripts.//tokens:digest: Rebuilds .altitude/ai-readiness/tokens-digest.json - the ground truth an agent verifies token claims against, and the source altitude_resolve_token reads. Derives every convention claim and all 601 token descriptions from the EMITTED bundles, so it cannot contradict the tree the way the hand-typed version did. Run after build:tokens; without it altitude_resolve_token is dead on a fresh clone.
scripts.//gate:api-vocabulary: API VOCABULARY RATCHET. The public prop vocabulary has to be predictable by a language model, and today it is not: `variant` does seven different jobs across 22 elements (emphasis, status, orientation, layout mode, SIZE, brand, shape), anchored placement is spelled four ways, and 44 booleans sit outside the is*/has* convention. This pins the measured violation count and fails in BOTH directions - a rise is a new violation, and a fall without --update means somebody fixed something and should tighten the pin. That two-way rule is the design against a ratchet that is seeded once and never turned. Canonical axes live in .altitude/api-vocabulary.json; the reasoning is .altitude/API-VOCABULARY.md.
scripts.//gate:cem-render: DOCUMENTED-API-THAT-DOES-NOT-EXIST GATE. Every @slot and @csspart in the CEM must actually be rendered by its component. The existing CEM gate checks that members are DOCUMENTED, never that documented members EXIST - so al-card advertised a slot `action-right` its render never emits, and the generated docs, the MCP and llms.txt all taught consumers an API that silently drops their content. Five real defects at the time of writing. Components whose template cannot be read statically are listed as NAMED skips, never guessed at.
scripts.//check:llms-content-type: Asserts the deployed machine artifacts arrive as text/plain and are not SPA shells. Takes a base URL; it is NOT part of any local gate, because a check that passes when nothing is deployed is the lie it exists to catch. Run it against a preview or production URL after a deploy.
scripts.//gate:token-usage: Fails on PHANTOM tokens only — a name read through var() that the pipeline never emits, so it silently falls back and its value is outside design-system control. DEAD tokens stay a report (see the script header): a tier-1 palette reserve is a legitimate design choice, a phantom never is. Reads styles/dist/tokens.json, so `build:tokens` is enough — no full build needed.
scripts.//generate:token-metadata: Spec 2026-08-22-token-debt-and-machine-readable-metadata (R7/R8/R9). MUTATES libs/al-web-components/styles/tokens-dtcg/**.json (the hand-authored DTCG source), writing a `$extensions` block per token. IDENTITY fields are read back and never recomputed: com.adobe.id uuid (generated once), com.atlassian.token introduced (a historical fact that must survive a file move — re-deriving it from git history at a renamed path silently resets it), and org.altitude.token cssType (the CSS surface the token is authored for; NOT recoverable from DTCG $type, which collapses sizing/spacing/borderRadius/borderWidth/fontSizes/lineHeights all into `dimension`). DERIVED fields are recomputed every run: org.primer.llm usage rules (authored per FAMILY, ~72 of them, inherited by every member — 552+ per-token prose would not be truthful), com.salesforce.styling cssProperties (derived from cssType, never fabricated), and com.atlassian.token state/replacement (state is only ever "deprecated" for the small, individually-verified list in scripts/lib/token-metadata-rules.mjs). A token with no cssType gets no cssProperties and is reported at the end of the run. Idempotent — safe to rerun after adding a token. See scripts/lib/dtcg-token.mjs for the two-types-per-token model, and gate:token-metadata for what enforces uuid stability.
scripts.//check:token-metadata: THE drift gate for the metadata generate:token-metadata writes — a generated artifact with no drift gate is the exact failure this spec keeps finding elsewhere. Asserts every token has a uuid, no two tokens share one, no existing token's uuid differs from what it was at HEAD (compares against `git show HEAD:<file>`, so there is no separate baseline file to rebaseline), and every `replacement` dot-path resolves to a real token. Run after generate:token-metadata or any manual edit to styles/tokens-dtcg/**.json. NOTE: files absent from HEAD compare against nothing — so immediately after the tokens/ -> tokens-dtcg/ move the uuid comparison reports 0 tokens and is a no-op. It re-arms on the first commit that contains the new paths.
scripts.//codemod:deprecated-tokens: Reads every `state: "deprecated"` token's `replacement` and scans real source for var() call sites. Same-CSS-property replacements (e.g. a duplicate alias) are rewritten with --write; cross-property replacements (e.g. a colour token superseded by an opacity token) are always just reported — a codemod that silently changes which CSS property a component sets is not safe. Dry run by default.
scripts.//skills:build: Regenerates .claude/skills/altitude-facts/GENERATED-FACTS.md (R10) — the mechanical half of the altitude-facts agent skill: component roster, per-tag doNotFlag caveats, token conventions/do-not-invent list and the MCP tool/resource/prompt roster, all read from the same committed artifacts llms.txt and the MCP capability matrix already read. The judgement half (SKILL.md) stays hand-written; see its §0.
scripts.//check:skills: Fails when .claude/skills/altitude-facts/GENERATED-FACTS.md has drifted from its sources — same discipline as check:llms and check:mcp-docs, applied to the agent skill instead of a doc page.
scripts.//check:ruleset-contexts: Are the main ruleset's required checks the jobs that actually run? GitHub matches a required check by its check-run NAME, and validates nothing: rename a job and the old context is still required, so the PR waits forever while every visible check is green. Add a job and forget the ruleset, and a red job blocks nothing. Both directions are checked. Needs the network (reads the live ruleset via gh) and falls back to the checked-in .github/rulesets/main.json, printing a NAMED not-verified line when neither is reachable.
